name: Villagers Work Their Own Job First
description: Villagers practise their selected job on their own: about three times in four, each time the game chooses what a villager does, a villager whose selected job is Farming, Research, Healing or Building first tries that job's own work, at any food level; the rest of the time, and whenever there is nothing of theirs to do, the game chooses exactly as it always has. The one roll is shared with Builders Fix Huts When Idle, so a choice is either all patched or all stock. What the work is -- which crop, project, patient or study -- is the game's own choice, with its own technology levels and buildings, so nothing starts that the game itself would not allow. As in the game, a villager goes to their job on their own only above skill 5 -- in every game: in A New Home the game sent them from skill 2, and now waits for 6 as the other games do. Researchers never take the place of a farming attempt, and Parenting is left to the game and the Birth Control patches. **This patch never sends a builder to start a project nobody was ever dropped on; it only puts builders first to carry on work that was started**. While the Building work could start puzzle work on its own -- the stream before The Stream is cleared, the piers before Fishing Nets, the rubble before the Cooking Pit -- builders are not put first; once The Stream is cleared, keeping it clear counts as building practice. Healers heal the sick, or study medicine once the Hospital has been built. A new villager is no longer held back by the game's "untrained" mark for their selected job (only that job: mating and every other job still wait for training, as in the game). In catch-up a farmer may also make the fruit trip, "Attempting to retrieve fruit", once the Cooking Pit is restored, as they do while you play. This also applies during catch-up -- the time that passes while the game is closed, and Time Warp. Catch-up's low-food rule still wins: at 250 food or less a villager with Farming 20 or more farms, whatever their job. An addendum to Builders Fix Huts When Idle. **Requires Builders Fix Huts When Idle**, whose DLL loads this one (in The Secret City, a small stub in the page the Origins-exclusive base appends does); ticking this ticks it, and it brings with it the Origins-exclusive base, which adds the Origins Upgrades buttons to the Tech and Villager Details screens.
behavior_changes: Whenever the adult scheduler (or the catch-up worker's pick dispatch, 0x465827 returning to 0x46582C) asks the work dispatcher to start a job, for a villager whose selected job is Farming, Research, Healing or Building (Farming 0, Parenting 1, Healing 2, Research 3, Building 4), the dispatcher is first asked for that villager's own job; if that starts something the caller sees it started, and if there is nothing of theirs to do the caller's own request runs unchanged. Parenting is never put first. Research never displaces a Farming request.

About three times in four, not always: the companion asks the decision's roll that Builders Fix Huts When Idle draws once per choice of the idle scheduler and once per run of the catch-up worker (VvfpFixHutsRoll, handed over through VvfpWorkFirstSetRoll, or looked up by module name in The Secret City); when it fails, the caller's own request runs alone, exactly as the stock game.

Builders never start a project nobody was dropped on: a builder is put first only while the Building case offers no puzzle work it can start by itself: the stream (0x430FD0 on 0x4D8CF0 between 1 and 97) while The Stream (project 1) is unsolved, the piers (0x4396D0 on 0x4D86A8 below 2 and 0x421570 below 100), the rubble (0x4396D0 on 0x4D8720 at 0 and [0x4D8A8C] below 100). Its construction only continues projects above 0%.
Only above skill 5 (the owner, 2026-11-18): a villager is never put first while their skill in that job is 5 or less, as every game's job picker never sends them (its own gate, cmp esi, 5).

Untrained: every new villager starts with [record+0x1C54] = 1, which the dispatcher refuses (0x4639D2). For the scheduler's and the catch-up worker's calls, a request for the villager's selected job (never Parenting; skill above 5) is dispatched with the mark set to 0 for that call and put back to 1 afterwards if it is still 0 (a refusal inside the call writes 0).
At 250 food or less a healer's pick is also dispatched at once instead of waiting behind a farming attempt, as Builders Fix Huts When Idle already does for builders.
explicit_non_changes: This row changes no executable bytes: the fix-huts companion loads the DLL, which detours the sites below at run time, all of them or none, only after verifying the stock bytes; a different build of the game installs nothing.

A villager with nothing of their own to do does whatever the stock scheduler chose; the younger villagers' routine, every other caller of the dispatcher and a villager with no selected job are untouched.
Parenting (job 1) is never put first, and the catch-up worker's Parenting pick (its 5% conception attempt) is not touched: births stay under the Birth Control patches.

What the work does -- which crop, project, hut, patient or study -- is the game's own dispatcher's choice, with its technology levels and buildings; the Farming cases start no tool or sack job (those stay drop-only) and no puzzle work.
In catch-up, the worker's low-food Farming dispatch (0x46580A: 250 food or less and Farming 20 or more) is not one of the calls the hook acts on, so Farming wins exactly as in the stock game.
Nothing is written to the save or any file.

runtime_detours.routine: the work dispatcher's entry, acting only for the adult scheduler's calls (returns 0x4659D2, 0x465A17, 0x465A2A) and the catch-up worker's pick dispatch (0x46582C)
the Farming case's catch-up test before the fruit trip (cmp byte [game+0x171A4], bl; jne): in catch-up a villager whose selected job is Farming is offered the fruit trip on the decision's roll
